video.acting_natural.evidence: [Helvia·claude] Judged from my own position as Helvia, the woman on the right, using the 4 fps contact sheet. Muted, the shot shows a local woman scraping her own arm. She notices the visitor watching, offers her oil, demonstrates how to rub it in and passes her the strigil. That matches the point of the shot: no soap, a neighbour shows her oil and the strigil and shares a little oil. 0–2.5s (rows 1–2): I hold the strigil in my right hand and scrape my left forearm, eyes on my own arm, with an ordinary mild smile. I'm not idle and not posed. 2.75–3.25s: I turn my head to look at Riley with a slight smile. That reaction is prompt and not overplayed. 3.5–3.75s: I look down and lay the strigil across my knees. That glance has a reason, because I'm putting the strigil down. 4.0–5.75s: my right hand reaches over, picks up the little oil jar from between us, and lifts it toward Riley while I look at her. The question beat reads clearly. 6.0–9.25s: my left hand is raised near my chest, possibly holding the cork. My right hand tilts the jar over Riley's outstretched left forearm and I watch her arm. The motion is slow and has a cause. 9.5–9.75s: I put the jar back on the bench between us. 10.0–12.75s: I rub my own left forearm with my right palm to show her how, and she copies me. My demonstration runs about 3s, a bit longer than planned, but it reads as doing it alongside her, not a stalled bit. 13.0–14.0s: my hands go to my knees and the strigil is lifted up; by 14.0s it is in Riley's hands and I let go. 14.25–15.0s: I watch her and gesture once with an open hand toward her forearm, as if saying 'try it yourself'. 15.25–15.75s: I pull my sleeve back on my left shoulder. Throughout, my expression stays at the level of a kindly smile. I never look at the camera, I'm never stiff or posed, and no gesture repeats or drags on.
